Article Title: India tour of New Zealand: Exposure for Test regulars to highlight selection meeting
Article Text:
Indian team head coach Gautam Gambhir, interacts with selectors RP Singh, Pragyan Ojha, Shiv Sundar Das and Ajay Ratra during the practice session ahead of the second ODI cricket match between India and West Indies, in Guwahati.

Ishan back in red-ball discussions

NEW DELHI: The India men's senior selection committee is likely to meet in the next 48 hours to pick the four squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. The meeting, which interim chief selector Pragyan Ojha is set to chair, was postponed from Monday because of Prasidh Krishna's pending fitness reports. The four selectors will soon get into a huddle to pick the T20I, ODI, Test and India A squads for the tour, which begins with the shortest format on October 22.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that since the A series, starting from October 24, overlaps with the T20Is and ODIs, the selectors are delicately handling the availability and exposure situation. While they don't want to dilute the two squads, providing red-ball exposure for Test regulars will be the top priority when they meet.Some India A bowlers might also stay back to assist the Test team with preparations. Spinners Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Vipraj Nigam and Shivang Kumar accompanied the Test team in Sri Lanka, and this time around, fast bowlers could well be asked to stay back in New Zealand after their A assignment.After his heroics in the Irani Cup fixture against Jammu & Kashmir, Mukesh Kumar is back on the selectors' radar and is likely to be drafted into the A squad for the three matches. Akash Deep will also be asked to play some games to be absolutely ready for the two Tests. The selectors are also deliberating on Jasprit Bumrah 's readiness. As TimesofIndia.com first reported, the management wants the fast bowler to increase his workload before joining the squad for the Wellington Test.The Ojha-led panel will be in a tight spot addressing the Bumrah situation, as asking the bowler to play one of the A fixtures could dilute their ODI attack. The option of a Ranji Trophy fixture was also on the table, but some decision-makers are uncomfortable with making him toil in the domestic circuit.It is understood that selectors have initiated plans to keep Ishan Kishan ready for the longest format. While they wanted him to feature in the A series, the overlapping of ODIs and T20Is could force them to look towards Dhruv Jurel and Kumar Kushagra. Rishabh Pant, who is playing only Tests now, is expected to complete his preparations by playing at least one A game.The left-hander will not be the only Test regular to do so, as KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan are all expected to feature in at least one fixture. Since KL will be part of the ODI squad, there is a strong possibility of him playing the first fixture from October 24 before joining the ODI squad in Auckland.Saransh Jain is unlikely to be considered with Washington Sundar back to full fitness, but the big question remains: how many spinners will the team carry? Ravindra Jadeja is expected to retain his spot in the playing XI, leaving the thinktank with the options of Manav Suthar and Kuldeep Yadav. It is unlikely that all four will board the flight, and the axe could fall on Kuldeep, considering the team's batting focus.More than a lot of spin-bowling all-rounders, it will make more sense to have someone like Nitish Kumar Reddy in the set-up, and there is a strong possibility of the management swaying his way.Too many quicks!Indian selectors will have a happy headache regarding the fast-bowling combination for the Tests. If all are fit and available, the onus will be on the selectors to choose the best-suited options from Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Akash Deep and Auqib Nabi. The scales, for now, heavily favour the first four, but an injury could open the door for either Nabi or Mukesh Kumar.The ODI depth will also be tested, as the Test regulars are likely to leave the squad for at least one fixture, if not both. Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Dhruv Jurel and Nitish Kumar Reddy could all be unavailable, which will force the selectors to reward consistent performers in the domestic and A circuits.Ruturaj Gaikwad, Kushagra and Naman Dhir will remain in the mix. Also watch out for Mayank Yadav, as he has been making a strong case for himself with his improved workload and ability to maintain his pace in long spells.
Article Summary: The India men's senior selection committee is likely to meet in the next 48 hours to pick the four squads for the upcoming tour of New Zealand. The meeting, which interim chief selector Pragyan Ojha is set to chair, was postponed from Monday because of Prasidh Krishna's pending fitness reports. India A bowlers might also stay back to assist the Test team with preparations.

Article Title: ‘He will dominate Indian cricket’: Shreyas Iyer’s big call on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi; Abhishek Sharma says ‘he belongs here’
Article Text:
Shreyas Iyer and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (Pic credit: BCCI)

‘Very silent, but on the field, very destructive’

Abhishek: ‘He belongs here’

Iyer wants winning to come first

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Fresh from their gold-medal-winning Asian Games campaign, Shreyas Iyer and Abhishek Sharma have returned to the home season with their focus already shifting towards the next generation of Indian cricket . Among the youngest members of the setup, 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has attracted plenty of attention — but Iyer believes the teenage sensation is still waiting for his opportunity to make a major impact.As India prepare to begin their five-match T20I series against the West Indies, Iyer opened up about his interactions with Sooryavanshi, revealing that their conversations often go beyond cricket. The India T20I captain said he deliberately tries to understand the teenager away from the sport, where the youngster is more comfortable being himself.Speaking on JioStar’s ‘Follow the Blues: Sarpanch Shreyas’, Iyer said he has enjoyed getting to know Sooryavanshi away from the pressures and expectations surrounding his cricket.“I keep interacting with Vaibhav in terms of what he does outside the field, because everyone talks to him about cricket, and we know how talented and gifted as an individual he is. So, just to talk about his lifestyle outside, that interaction, knowing about his family, what he does, what not, that excites him more because he’s more of himself when he talks about it,” Iyer said.The contrast between Sooryavanshi’s personality away from cricket and his aggressive approach with the bat has also caught the captain's attention.“And a very silent guy, but on the field, is very destructive. So, that’s like an irony when you look at him. He’s a very charming, sweet guy to interact with and good to have him around the dressing room,” Iyer added.While Sooryavanshi remains part of the squad, Iyer stressed that the youngster has to wait for his opportunity, with India's established World Cup-winning openers currently ahead of him in the pecking order.“And I know that his time will come, because we have been playing with World Cup-winning openers right now, and they deserve the time out there and he’s still in the 15. So definitely, when his time comes, he is going to dominate Indian cricket,” Iyer said.Abhishek, who was also part of India's Asian Games gold-medal-winning campaign, echoed Iyer's belief in Sooryavanshi's potential while emphasising the importance of making the teenager comfortable inside the dressing room.The left-handed opener said Sooryavanshi is already more accustomed to the demands of professional cricket than most teenagers his age, having spent several years in the cricket system.“He is a very smart guy. He is not like how we used to behave at 15 or anyone does because he has already been in that cricket setup for 2-3 years. So he knows what, where, and how much to practice. I feel gradually these are things he will learn more with experience. And what we discuss in the team with each other, all teammates, is how we can make him more comfortable,” Abhishek told JioStar.The 26-year-old also believes the responsibility lies with the senior players to ensure that Sooryavanshi does not feel overwhelmed by the attention surrounding his rapid rise.“Because we all know what he has achieved and that he belongs here. So I also feel like it’s my duty as well, to make him feel that all of us, his elder brothers, are here for him. You just have to enjoy and just give your best and win the games whenever you get the chance,” he added.While the emergence of youngsters such as Sooryavanshi offers India an opportunity to build depth, Iyer made it clear that experimentation will not come at the cost of results.“The most important thing for me is to win the series, and then we can experiment with the playing combination. Experimenting from the start doesn’t make sense because then the players also get insecure, and then they start questioning themselves, questioning others around the dressing room. And then they go in that dilemma phase where they feel like, ‘Will I get a match ahead or will I not get one?’ I don’t like that mindset. I’ve been in that mindset in the past, and I know how it feels from inside,” Iyer said.The West Indies series therefore marks the beginning of another phase for India, with the Asian Games gold medal now behind them and the focus shifting towards building a settled, confident side.
Article Summary: Shreyas Iyer and Abhishek Sharma speak to JioStar's ‘Follow the Blues: Sarpanch Shreyas’ Iyer believes 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is still waiting for his opportunity to make a major impact. The India T20I captain said he deliberately tries to understand the teenager away from the sport, where the youngster is more comfortable.

Article Title: 'I had fever, was not high on energy': R Praggnanandhaa after double medals at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive
Article Text:
R Praggnanandhaa talks about his Chess Olympiad campaign

Fever, fatigue, and fighting through it

R Praggnanandhaa at 2026 Chess Olympiad (Photo by Michal Walusza for FIDE)

A personal campaign that read better than the scoreline

R Praggnanandhaa plays against Anish Giri (Photo by Michal Walusza for FIDE)

Where the gold went missing

Srinath Narayanan waits for Nihal Sarin's game to end (Photo by Michal Walusza for FIDE)

I've been playing how I want to play. I've been enjoying playing the games, and I think it's also showing in the results. R Praggnanandhaa, Indian Grandmaster

Candidates in the rearview, Clutch Chess ahead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In the open section of the 2026 Candidates Tournament, Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa was India's sole representative in Cyprus earlier this year. He did not win the top prize there. But the quality of chess he played was unmistakably high.He has continued to maintain that standard at every tournament since, and the results have simply followed.Despite being last at one point at Norway Chess, he made a remarkable comeback, beating five-time world champion and world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen twice on his home soil to become the first Indian ever to lift that coveted title in June More recently, he became the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour. Coming into the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, nobody thus questioned his place as India's Board 1 player.And although he could manage only three wins from his 10 games during India's silver-and-bronze campaign, a tally that brought him an individual bronze medal too, there was never a lack of quality on show from the 21-year-old Chennai-born grandmaster."His score (6.5/10) still didn't completely reflect the level at which he played. He created chances in almost every game, quite a few draws which could have been wins. But the quality of his play was really high," captain Srinath Narayanan told TimesofIndia.com after the campaign . "It never looked like Pragg was in danger of losing. Even the couple of times he fought into slightly worse positions, body-language-wise, he was the one pushing.His opponents were the ones who were a bit stressed."The Uzbekistan Olympiad, though, wasn't an ideal one healthwise for much of the Indian contingent, and Pragg was among those who had to battle it out while under the weather."I'm recovering," he told this website, when asked if he was back to full health after the gruelling tournament, which had only one rest day. "The last few days I was having some cold and a little fever as well at some point. So I wasn't high on energy towards the end of the tournament. But it kind of got better after the tournament ended. The last few days have been better. I'm also getting good sleep, so it's fine."There was an obvious question about conditions, food, or the weather in Samarkand. Pragg waved most of that away. "I think the conditions were extremely good. The first day, we had a little inconvenience. But after that, the Uzbek Chess Federation arranged a private place for the Indian team to have their own dinner. We got the Indian food from the AICF, thanks to AICF, and we could keep it in this place. Generally, I think the overall arrangements after the first day were really good, thanks to AICF and the Uzbek Federation as well. "So what was behind the string of illnesses, if not the food or the travel?"It was not a problem with any of those. I think it's just that something was maybe spreading among the players. I think it started with someone and then everyone towards the end got it." Asked if it was simply a viral fever making the rounds, he agreed. "Yeah, probably like viral fever that was spreading. I heard that even before the tournament, in my area and stuff, there were people who were getting it. But we were all fine in the first half of the tournament. It was mainly in the second half that these things started."It's rare, he insisted, for it to catch up with him specifically. "In general, I try not to experiment too much during a tournament. I go with my comfort food. I don't do something that brings a cold — even something like going out in the cold can trigger it. We also take medicines that usually don't make you sleepy, so you can be prepared in such a way. But generally, these things don't happen during a tournament. For me, I don't know when the last time was that I had a cold during a tournament. I can't really think of it. These things are rare for all the players. We're generally able to avoid these things, but it happens in some tournaments. Sometimes it's not in your control."On the board, Pragg's own account of his Olympiad matched what his captain had already said. "For me, I think I played well. Overall, the quality was okay. Most of the games I was pushing, I was the one creating a lot of chances. I think the only two games where I was worse were against Anish (Giri) and Rapport (Richard) in the last game. But it was only for a few moves. It's not like I had to defend for a long time. It was just a few moves, and then the position changed. Either I was fine or I was taking over."Where it stung was in the games he should have put away. "Given the chances I had, I could have, should have probably scored one or two wins more. Some games it was surprising how I missed. For example, the match against Spain, against Anton, I missed a completely winning position. That was kind of surprising to me as well. But these things happen in sports. Sometimes you convert these things effortlessly, but sometimes you also miss these chances. It all happens," the 21-year-old GM remarked.Zoom out to the team picture, and Pragg is unambiguous about where the Olympiad was decided and at peace with how it ended."I think silver is a good result. Obviously, after coming from a gold medal last year and the way we won gold, there was an expectation from everyone, also from the players, that you're coming from such a high and you want to keep it. You want to win gold again. Obviously, repeating that performance is difficult, but you want to win gold again. But there are other strong teams, so it's not going to be easy every time. I think, in that way, silver is a good result. Given how strong the Olympiad was and how many close matches we had, I think silver is a good result," Praggnanandhaa explained.One match, though, decided it."Obviously, the critical match was against Uzbekistan. I think it's going to be the critical match in every Olympiad to come, because we're all strong players and we're all young, so there are going to be a lot of Olympiads where we will face each other. It's going to be interesting. But obviously, that match was the critical one," he said.Explaining what actually went wrong in it, he continued, "The Uzbek team also knew this was going to be like a final, because whoever wins has a massive advantage. One unfortunate moment ( the queen blunder in Nihal Sarin's game against Uzbekistan ) for us cost us the match, and these things happen in a tournament. But I felt overall, in that match, we were all playing well. Our game quality was really good. All of us were pressing at some point. We were not worse at any moment. There were no boards where we were in danger."One blunder can happen at any stage of a tournament, to anyone. I can show every top player blundering in some crucial game. It happens, and it's unfortunate that it happened at this moment. Obviously, it was difficult for all of us, but I think we all stood as a team. I think we recovered from that."Padel sessions between games, he added with a laugh, helped more than people might assume, "Yeah, I mean, especially for Nihal, it was more difficult, but I think we all managed to stay as a team, and I think we all are recovered now."The Olympiad arrives roughly five months after Pragg's own campaign at the Candidates in Cyprus fell short of the world title shot, a result that, by his own admission, shaped much of his year."It's been good these last few months. But obviously, I think the crucial tournament was the Candidates Tournament, which was a disappointment. After that, I felt my play has generally been good. I've been playing how I want to play.I've been enjoying playing the games, and I think it's also showing in the results."Does the Candidates setback still linger? "Not too much. I think these results do help in getting out of it completely. But of course, when you think about the future, Candidates is the main thing."For now, the schedule doesn't leave much room to dwell on it anyway. Pragg is already looking at his next two stops: Clutch Chess in the US, starting October 27, followed by the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot event in Budapest on November 10.A fever-interrupted Olympiad behind him, a title shot still unfinished business ahead, Praggnanandhaa feels his story has just begun.
Article Summary: Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa was India's sole representative in Cyprus earlier this year. He has continued to maintain that standard at every tournament since, and the results have simply followed. The Uzbekistan Olympiad wasn't an ideal one healthwise for the Indian contingent.

Article Title: IND vs WI: Why India and West Indies were fined after 3rd ODI
Article Text:
India vs West Indies 3rd ODI (ANI Photo/Rahul Singh)

West Indies end ODI series on a high

India and the West Indies have been fined for maintaining slow over-rates during the third and final ODI of their three-match series in New Chandigarh on Saturday.India were four overs behind the required rate after time allowances were taken into account, while the West Indies were two overs short. As a result, India were fined 20 per cent of their match fee, while the West Indies received a 10 per cent fine."In accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time," the ICC said in a statement.Both captains accepted the charges and the proposed sanctions, meaning there was no need for a formal hearing.The penalties were imposed by Prakash Bhatt of the ICC International Panel of Match Referees.On-field umpires Jayaraman Madanagopal and Sam Nogajski, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Virender Sharma had levelled the charges.The West Indies had already lost the three-match series 2-0 before the final ODI, but they finished the series with a memorable win.Led by an unbeaten 162 from captain Shai Hope, the visitors successfully chased down 352, recording their highest successful run chase in ODI cricket.Their previous best was 331/5 against Ireland in 2019.Hope also created history with his innings. He became the first wicketkeeper-captain to score more than 150 runs in an ODI innings.His knock was also the highest score by a West Indies men's batter in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Brian Lara's 153 against Pakistan in Sharjah in 1993.With the ODI series now over, India and the West Indies will shift their focus to the five-match T20I series, which begins on Tuesday.
Article Summary: India and the West Indies have been fined for maintaining slow over-rates. India were four overs behind the required rate after time allowances were taken into account. The West Indies were two overs short. Both captains accepted the charges and proposed sanctions, meaning there was no need for a formal hearing.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was India's youngest medallist; do you know who was the oldest?
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Mairaj Ahmad Khan

Vaibhav becomes India’s youngest medallist

Mairaj makes history at 50

The Asian Games 2026 took place in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4, with athletes from 46 nations competing across various sports. India finished fourth in the medal table with 85 medals, including 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes.India enjoyed several memorable performances, with the men’s and women’s teams winning gold medals in cricket, kabaddi and hockey. It was also the first time both Indian hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games Among the standout individual performers was 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod, who became the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold.She finished the Games with two golds and a silver. Pranavi Urs also created history by winning India’s first individual golf gold, while Neeru Dhanda became the country’s first women’s trap shooting gold medallist.At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became India’s youngest-ever Asian Games gold medallist. The teenage batting sensation was part of the Indian men’s cricket team that defeated Pakistan by 19 runs in the final to win gold.Sooryavanshi made an aggressive start, hitting two consecutive sixes, before Saim Ayub dismissed him for 15 off nine balls. Despite his early exit, India went on to win the final and secure a memorable gold medal.Two-time Olympian Mairaj Ahmad Khan became India’s oldest medallist at the 2026 Asian Games at the age of 50. He won bronze as part of the men’s skeet shooting team alongside Anantjeet Singh Naruka and Bhavtegh Singh Gill.Khan has competed internationally for more than 20 years and is a three-time ISSF World Cup gold medallist. However, the bronze in Aichi-Nagoya was his first Asian Games medal.Overall, Japan’s 11-year-old eSports player Yuki Kurihara became the youngest gold medallist in Asian Games history after winning the Puyo Puyo Champions title. Kuwait’s 63-year-old shooter Abdullah Al-Rashidi was the oldest medallist overall, winning silver in men’s skeet.
Article Summary: The Asian Games 2026 took place in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from September 19 to October 4. India finished fourth in the medal table with 85 medals, including 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes. Among the standout individual performers was 17-year-old archer Kumkum Mohod, who became the first Indian woman to win individual recurve gold.

Article Title: New beginnings, new heroes: Women lead India's charge as a new generation shines in Nagoya
Article Text:
Lovlina Borgohain and Neeru Dhanda (Image credit: X)

The comeback girls

Golden standards

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As Neeru Dhanda led the Indian contingent out for one last time at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday night, it was symbolic of how India’s Asian Games campaign had unfolded over the past two weeks.The women had come to the fore - packing punches, vaulting to new heights, lifting weights, taking aim, towering over opponents with sixes, blazing the track, finding the fairway and hitting the back of the net. India’s final tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, may represent a drop from the 106 medals and 28 golds won in Hangzhou. But numbers alone cannot tell the story of these Games.There were path-breakers everywhere, athletes who pushed through glass ceilings that had stood for years. The aftermath will bring reviews, reflections, deliberations and reports. But before the analysis begins, it is only fair to celebrate those who made these Games count.For almost 12 days, the Indian gold rush had remained subdued. Then, just as the sun finally began showing up in Nagoya, the floodgates opened. Eleven gold medals came in the final two days, transforming what had threatened to become a disappointing campaign into a collection of stories about guts, resilience and glory.Dhanda, the 26-year-old from Sangatpura in Haryana, had set the tone by winning India’s first individual gold of these Games in the women’s trap event. The women went on to win 11 gold medals, apart from the three secured in mixed events.The contingent had 83 debutants, who accounted for 41 of India’s 85 medals — a clear indication of a changing guard across several sports.But if one athlete were to be picked as the face of that change, it would be difficult to look beyond 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod. The Maharashtra archer won two gold medals and a silver, but her biggest achievement went beyond the medal tally.She ended South Korea’s two-decade domination of the women’s recurve events by becoming the first Indian to win individual recurve gold at the Asian Games. It did not take her long to make the biggest stage of her young career her own.Even her Korean opponent Oh Ye-jin, whom Kumkum beat for the individual gold, was left impressed. “For a 17-year-old, she is very composed and has a very bright future,” Oh said.Another teenager, Prithika Pradeep, also emerged with two gold medals, adding to the sense that a new generation is beginning to announce itself. Pranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an Asian Games golf gold.Behind every medal was a story of humble beginnings, survival in sport, societal pressures overcome and personal tragedies endured. That made the successes more than just entries in a medal table.They were not newcomers to the big stage. They had competed at the biggest of them all — the Olympics. But Nagoya offered unfinished business.Lovlina Borgohain had contemplated walking away from boxing after a difficult phase post the 2024 Paris Olympics. Instead, she returned to punch her way to gold.Parveen Hooda, returning after a doping ban, produced her own golden comeback. The bronze she had won in Hangzhou and subsequently lost became gold in Nagoya. Mirabai Chanu did not win gold, but her silver in the 49kg category had the weight of a champion’s achievement. It also completed her Asian Games medal collection.The women’s kabaddi team survived a tense battle against Iran. The women’s hockey team ended a 44-year wait for Asian Games gold. And Harmanpreet Kaur and her team ensured that cricket’s gold returned to India.Among the men, too, there were performances that demanded attention — Aman Sehrawat in wrestling, Ankush Panghal in boxing and Gulveer Singh in long-distance running among them.Yet, for all the celebration, there were glaring blanks. Manu Bhaker, one of India’s biggest sporting heroes, returned without a medal.There were plenty of nearmisses and some disastrous outings. India’s badminton return of a solitary bronze was another disappointment, particularly with a strong men’s doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen in the squad.Table tennis also raised questions, while equestrian had its own share of run-ins between administrators and riders, alongside selectionrelated concerns but failed to add to the medal count.
Article Summary: India's final tally of 85 medals, including 21 gold, may represent a drop from the 106 medals and 28 golds won in Hangzhou. But numbers alone cannot tell the story of these Games. There were path-breakers everywhere, athletes who pushed through glass ceilings that had stood for years.

Article Title: 'You can't just depend on Japrit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya': Ex-India cricketer urges veteran pacers' return ahead of 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
Hardik Pandya and Jasprit Bumrah

‘Team is going backwards’

Former India batter Hanuma Vihari has called on the team to bring experienced pacers Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Shami back into the ODI setup. His comments came after India failed to defend 351 against the West Indies in the third ODI, losing by five wickets.Vihari believes India need more reliable bowling options instead of depending heavily on Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya for wickets, especially with the 2027 ODI World Cup less than a year away.Bhuvneshwar last played an ODI for India in 2022, with injuries affecting his career. However, the 36-year-old has remained effective in the IPL, taking 45 wickets in 30 matches across the 2025 and 2026 seasons for Royal Challengers Bengaluru.“I think they have to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back. In my opinion, he is still one of the best bowlers in the country. He is proving in the IPL," Vihari said on his YouTube channel.Vihari feels Bhuvneshwar's experience and control with the new ball could give India greater stability. He also believes Shami should return to strengthen the attack.“You cannot just depend on Bumrah and Hardik. You have to have backup in case of such injuries. I will say go with experience. Get Bhuvneshwar and Shami back," he said. “You will have some security with experience.When you need a breakthrough, you can go to them, and they will do the job for you. You need stability and experience will always count."Vihari described India's failure to defend a total above 350 as a major warning sign. The West Indies chased down 351 in 48.2 overs, exposing concerns about India's bowling, particularly on flat pitches.“We could not defend 350. Is this not a wake-up call? I think the team is going backwards. This is a big blow," he said.He also raised concerns over India's backup bowlers after expensive spells from Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar and Nitish Kumar Reddy.“The West Indies exposed the Indian bowling attack. They are not even part of the World Cup. Imagine top teams like Australia, South Africa, England," Vihari added.
Article Summary: Hanuma Vihari calls on India to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Mohammed Shami back into the ODI setup. The 36-year-old last played an ODI for India in 2022. He has remained effective in the IPL, taking 45 wickets in 30 matches across the 2025 and 2026 seasons for Royal Challengers Bengaluru. India failed to defend 351 against the West Indies in the third ODI.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal return possible? Head coach Jorge Jesus clears the air on 41-year-old's future
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly left Portugal after Jesus allegedly broke promises over his Norway warm-up, with a private apology replaced by public defiance/ Image: X

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Portugal still counting on Ronaldo

Portugal coach Jorge Jesus has kept the door open for Cristiano Ronaldo to return to the national team after the 41-year-old captain left the squad last week. Ronaldo departed after being left on the bench against Norway and told he would not start against Denmark, later saying he would explain his decision "in due course"."If he wants to, he'll return to the national team. We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one who's going to decide," Jesus said, as quoted by news agency Reuters, after Portugal beat Norway 2-1."He's the one who should decide how he wants to end his time with the national team. In my first call-up, I said, 'I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you'. And now I'm saying the same thing."Portugal won without Ronaldo against Denmark before beating Norway to reach the Nations League quarter-finals. Ronaldo remains the country's record scorer and most-capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca also said Ronaldo remains part of the team's plans and described his departure as a misunderstanding that should be handled internally."He is in the national team on sporting merit, and that must be unquestionable," Proenca told RTP. "We have to pay tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo."Jesus, who previously coached Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, expects the forward could return during the next international break if he chooses. Portugal will host Denmark on November 14 before travelling to Wales three days later.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo could return to the Portugal squad, says coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo left the squad last week after being left on the bench against Denmark. Portugal won without Ronaldo against Denmark before beating Norway to reach the Nations League quarter-finals. Ronaldo remains the country's record scorer and most-capped player.

Article Title: ‘Farewell he truly deserves’: Lionel Messi joins Argentina camp ahead of emotional swansong
Article Text:
Lionel Messi will play his final game for Argentina (File Photo)

Argentina stars set for Messi tribute

Messi’s next chapter

Lionel Messi has joined the Argentina squad ahead of what is expected to be his final international appearance on home soil. The 39-year-old forward arrived at the team’s Ezeiza training base on Sunday and took part in his first session before the squad gathered for a traditional asado.Argentina will face Benin at the Estadio Monumental on Tuesday, with around 85,000 fans expected to attend the special occasion. The team enters the game in strong form after beating Bolivia 4-0 and Burkina Faso 7-0.Messi will enter the farewell match with an impressive record of 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina. His international career includes winning the 2022 World Cup, two Copa America titles and the Finalissima.AFA president Claudio Tapia explained why the federation decided to organise the special event, saying: "We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on October 6 here in Argentina."Several of Messi’s long-time teammates will be there for his final appearance. Giovani Lo Celso, Rodrigo De Paul and Nicolas Otamendi are expected to play alongside the Argentina captain.Leandro Paredes will also attend the event from the stands despite serving a 10-match FIFA suspension following the 2026 World Cup final.However, two members of Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad, Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina, will miss the occasion. Their club, AS Roma, did not allow them to travel.Argentina will wear a special one-off kit for the occasion, featuring the Sun of May and laurel branches around Messi’s famous No. 10.After the match, Messi will return his focus to club football with Inter Miami, where he is contracted until the end of the 2028 MLS season.For Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni, the farewell also marks the beginning of a new phase as he looks to develop the next generation of players for the team’s upcoming tournament cycle.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi has joined the Argentina squad ahead of what is expected to be his final international appearance on home soil. The 39-year-old forward arrived at the team’s Ezeiza training base on Sunday and took part in his first session. Argentina will face Benin at the Estadio Monumental on Tuesday, with around 85,000 fans expected to attend.

Article Title: 33 teams, no relegation, 198 matches: Mumbai football's Elite Division raises eyebrows
Article Text:
MFA Elite Division raises eyebrows

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Mumbai’s top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions, and not necessarily for the right reasons.The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams, a number virtually unheard of for a top division. What’s more, there will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.The bloated league is the result of the MFA’s decision to merge its Private and Corporate leagues. The Corporate league had complained of being treated as a second-class competition, with poor scheduling and matches often confined to barely three months, making it difficult for companies such as Western Railway and Indian Navy to commit teams. Rather than address those concerns, the MFA opted for a merger.The 33 teams will be split into three groups of 11, with the top four from each advancing to a playoff stage comprising two groups of six. The top four will then enter the semifinals and final. In all, 198 matches will need to be staged.But venues and scheduling pose another concern. While the MFA is fighting to retain the Neville D’Souza ground, it has secured Cooperage for matches.At time slots of 10 am and 12 noon! When Mumbai’s heat and humidity are at their peak. AFC A-licensed coach Raj Shekar told TOI: “We must consider Mumbai’s heat and humidity and whether this is sustainable for players, clubs and spectators if we want to make the league popular.Shekar also questioned the 51.5% increase in the entry fee, saying it had, to his understanding, neither been approved by the president nor placed before the executive committee.Ex-India captain Godfrey Pereira was blunt: “It’s an absolute mess and definitely not something that should happen. How will it help grow the sport? Without relegation, what’s there to fight? The quality will deteriorate.”Sudhakar Rane, MFA secretary, told TOI that it’s the best they could do. “Teams in the corporate league were complaining, so we thought that this was the best solution. About the ground, these slots were the only ones available so there’s nothing we can do about it.”
Article Summary: Mumbai's top-flight football league is set to enter a season of unprecedented proportions. The Mumbai Football Association’s (MFA) Elite Division, which kicks off on Oct 15, will feature 33 teams. There will be no relegation for three years. At the end of that period, the division could have as many as 39 teams.

Article Title: India win men's compound team gold, archery haul grows to three golds at Asian Games

NEW DELHI: India continued their strong run in archery at the Asian Games 2026 as the trio of Kushal Dalal, Sahil Jadhav and Ganesh Mani Ratnam won the gold medal in the men's compound team event in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Wednesday.The Indian team defeated China 238-237 in a thrilling final to clinch the gold medal.India held their nerve in a closely fought contest.The men's compound team gold came on a big day for Indian archery.Earlier, the women's compound team of Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep also won gold after beating China 238-234 in the final.India's compound mixed team of Chikitha and Sahil also finished on top after beating South Korea in a shoot-off. Article Summary: Kushal Dalal, Sahil Jadhav and Ganesh Mani Ratnam win gold in men's compound team event. Indian team defeated China 238-237 in a thrilling final to clinch the gold medal. Earlier, Indian women's team also won gold after beating China in the final.

Article Title: 'Real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh lead cricket fraternity in hailing Captain Smit Machchhar after saving 174 lives
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar

'A true real-life hero': Sachin Tendulkar

Raina hails 'son of Gujarat'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sehwag praises his courage under pressure

Yuvraj: 'Some moments show you what a person is truly made of'

NEW DELHI: The courage of Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073, has earned admiration from across the country, including some of India's biggest cricketing names.Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag were among the former India cricketers who took to social media to salute Machchhar for his bravery and presence of mind during the terrifying mid-air incident.Machchhar was the captain of the Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight when a violent confrontation reportedly broke out in the cockpit on Wednesday. According to reports, he was attacked by his co-pilot but, despite suffering serious injuries, managed to help open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew members to intervene. The aircraft was subsequently diverted and landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 174 people aboard were reported safe.Tendulkar was among the first prominent cricketers to acknowledge Machchhar's courage."Learnt about the incredible bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar. Immense courage in the face of a terrifying and unprecedented challenge. A true real-life hero. The entire world is proud of you," Tendulkar wrote.Former India batter Suresh Raina also paid tribute to Machchhar, highlighting the captain's courage despite being seriously injured."A true hero, a proud moment for India! Salute to Captain Smit Machchhar, a son of Gujarat, whose extraordinary courage and presence of mind, even while seriously injured, helped save 174 precious lives," Raina wrote.Virender Sehwag highlighted the extraordinary circumstances in which Machchhar continued to act despite his injuries."In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others," Sehwag wrote.Yuvraj Singh also joined the tributes, focusing on Machchhar's decision to put the safety of others ahead of his own."Some moments show you what a person is truly made of," Yuvraj wrote.Machchhar, who has more than 13 years of commercial flying experience and previously worked with SpiceJet before joining flydubai in 2022, is currently recovering after undergoing treatment in Saudi Arabia.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured while trying to prevent a potential catastrophe aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073. Sachin Tendulkar, Yuvraj Singh, Suresh Raina and Virender Sehwag took to social media to pay tribute to the pilot's bravery. All 174 people aboard the flight were reported safe.

Article Title: SA20: Faf du Plessis, Rassie van der Dussen headline auction shortlist
Article Text:

How things stand ahead of SA20 Auction.

The SA20 Season 5 auction will see 156 cricketers go under the hammer on October 7, with former Joburg Super Kings captain Faf du Plessis Rassie van der Dussen and all-rounder Wiaan Mulder among the leading South African names available.The shortlist was trimmed down from 789 players who initially registered for the auction. Of the 156 players remaining, 95 are South African and 61 are overseas cricketers, with 19 squad places still available across four of the six franchises.Durban's Super Giants and Paarl Royals have already completed their 19-player squads and will not participate in the auction. Joburg Super Kings and MI Cape Town have six slots each to fill, while Pretoria Capitals have five and Sunrisers Eastern Cape have two.JSK and MI Cape Town also have the largest purses available, with $1.24 million and $562,813, respectively. Sunrisers Eastern Cape have $216,699 remaining, while Pretoria Capitals have $88,786.Among the leading South African players in the pool are du Plessis, Mulder, fast bowler Nandre Burger and veteran batter van der Dussen. Du Plessis, who previously led JSK, continues to feature prominently in franchise cricket and recently finished as the leading run-scorer in Europe.The two Under-23 slots are also expected to attract significant interest. Fast bowler Matthew Boast, who commanded the joint-highest bid at the Season 2 auction, is among the players in this category, alongside former South Africa Under-19 captain Jason Rowles.The first four SA20 auctions have produced several significant deals. Tristan Stubbs fetched $554,693 at the inaugural auction, while Dewald Brevis set a new record with a $994,834 deal last season.The auction has also provided a route for several South African players to gain exposure to international franchise cricket, with some subsequently securing further opportunities on the global T20 circuit.The overseas contingent includes former West Indies captain Kieron Pollard, New Zealand pacer Trent Boult, Shimron Hetmyer, Shamar Joseph, Mohammad Nabi, AM Ghazanfar, Jordan Cox, Aneurin Donald, Rehan Ahmed and Richard Gleeson.Several established T20 names are already part of the six franchises, including Jos Buttler, Joe Root, Sam Curran, Sunil Narine, Kane Williamson, Andre Russell, Sherfane Rutherford, Mitchell Marsh and Phil Salt.The auction will be broadcast live on SuperSport at 5pm SAST, JioStar at 8.30pm IST, Sky Sports at 4pm BST, Apex at 7.30pm PKT, Fox Sports at 11pm AEDT and Willow TV at 11am ET. The event will also be streamed live on the SA20 YouTube channel.
Article Summary: The SA20 Season 5 auction will see 156 cricketers go under the hammer on October 7. Former Joburg Super Kings captain Faf du Plessis and all-rounder Wiaan Mulder are among the leading South African names available. Of the 156 players remaining, 95 are South African and 61 are overseas.

MUMBAI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ) has deputed a three-member selection committee, headed by former India seamer Harvinder Singh and including ex-first-class cricketers Sridharan Sharath (Tamil Nadu) and Amitabh Vijayvargiya (Madhya Pradesh), to Bihar to pick the squad for the upcoming Ranji Trophy , which will kick off on October 11, TOI has learnt.Harvinder and Sharath, who was also the junior chief selector, have been senior national selectors in the past.To pick Bihar's junior teams for the BCCI's various age-group tournaments — Under-16, Under-19 and Under-23 — the BCCI has formed a three-member selection committee comprising ex-national junior selector Harvinder Singh Sodhi, former Punjab allrounder Krishan Mohan and former Gujarat wicketkeeper Pathik Patel.“All the selectors have reached Patna today and begun their work of identifying talented local cricketers at the Moin-Ul-Haq Stadium in Patna,” a source tracking developments said.On September 16, the Supreme Court appointed former Patna High Court judge Justice Ashwani Kumar Singh as the administrator of the Bihar Cricket Association (BCA).Before the last season too, the BCCI had appointed a four-member selection committee to pick various age-group teams for the Board's tournaments.That committee included former India chief selector Chetan Sharma, Harvinder Singh, ex-India pacer Salil Ankola, and former India women's team left-arm spinner and national chief selector Neetu David.Promoted to the Elite Group, Bihar will take on Uttar Pradesh in their Ranji Trophy opener at Rajgir. Article Title: West Indies name Amit Jangoo as replacement for injured Jewel Andrew

West Indies' Amir Jangoo. (PTI Photo/Ravi Choudhary)

Impressive ODI form

The West Indies have added wicketkeeper-batter Amit Jangoo to their squad for the upcoming T20I series against India. He has been brought in as cover for Jewel Andrew, who suffered a finger injury during the third ODI in New Chandigarh on Saturday.Andrew was injured while taking a catch to dismiss India batter Naman Dhir. The wicketkeeper immediately left the field and was taken to hospital for an X-ray as the West Indies medical team assessed the extent of the injury. Cricket West Indies said, "Amir Jangoo has been added to the squad as cover for the wicketkeeping position following the finger injury sustained by Jewel Andrew during Saturday’s third ODI. Andrew is still being monitored and assessed by the medical team."Andrew picked up the injury on the final delivery of the 36th over of India's innings. Dhir chipped a delivery from left-arm spinner Gudakesh Motie towards cover, where Andrew completed the catch but took a heavy blow to his finger.The injury meant Andrew could not open the innings during the West Indies' chase of 352. Skipper Shai Hope was moved up the order, replacing John Campbell at the top.Jangoo, 29, has already played seven T20Is for the West Indies since making his international debut in December 2024.He has scored 163 runs in the format at a strike rate of 120.74.The wicketkeeper-batter comes into the T20I series after an excellent ODI campaign against India. Jangoo scored an unbeaten 58, followed by 114 and 67 in the three matches.His total of 239 runs made him the third-highest run-scorer in the ODI series across both teams. Only India's Shubman Gill, with 334 runs, and West Indies captain Shai Hope, with 278, scored more.The first T20I between India and West Indies will be played in Lucknow on Tuesday.
Article Summary: West Indies have added wicketkeeper-batter Amit Jangoo to their squad for the upcoming T20I series against India. He has been brought in as cover for Jewel Andrew, who suffered a finger injury during the third ODI in New Chandigarh on Saturday. Andrew was injured while taking a catch to dismiss India batter Naman Dhir.

A bizarre moment during the Canada's premier T10 cricket league semi-final between Toronto Sixers and Mississauga Masters left players, commentators and fans surprised.A delivery from USA pacer Ali Khan flew over the batter and wicketkeeper before landing in the stands, but Toronto were awarded only five runs instead of six.Toronto had posted 130/4 in 10 overs, with Kieron Pollard smashing 40 from 16 balls. During the ninth over, Khan bowled a bouncer that went over Pollard and the wicketkeeper before clearing the boundary without touching the bat.The commentators initially thought it would be a wide and six. However, the umpire awarded five runs to Toronto. Under MCC laws, a six can only be given when the ball has been hit by the bat.Watch:According to Law 19.7, if a ball crosses the boundary without being struck by the bat, it is treated as a boundary four. Since the delivery was also a wide, the additional one-run wide penalty is added, making it five runs in total.Despite the unusual incident, Toronto Sixers went on to beat Mississauga Masters by nine runs and secure their place in the final. Mississauga put up a strong chase, led by Alex Lees, who smashed 39 off just 11 balls, but they could not complete the chase.In the other semi-final, Vancouver Anchors defeated Brampton Blitz by six wickets. They will now face Toronto Sixers in the tournament final.
Article Summary: A delivery from USA pacer Ali Khan flew over the batter and wicketkeeper before landing in the stands. Under MCC laws, a six can only be given when the ball has been hit by the bat. Toronto Sixers went on to beat Mississauga Masters by nine runs and secure their place in the final.

The defining moment of the Irani Cup clash between Ranji Trophy champions Jammu & Kashmir and Rest of India came on Sunday at the Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium.Chasing 279, J&K were 65/2 when Bengal pacer Mukesh Kumar urged stand-in RoI captain Sarfaraz Khan — regular skipper Rishabh Pant was on the sidelines with fever — to give him one more over. Mukesh made it count.In the 13th over, he trapped Shubham Pundir lbw for 9 with a delivery that jagged back in, with Sarfaraz taking a successful review after the umpire had ruled it not out. He then bowled J&K captain Paras Dogra, their first-innings top-scorer with 75, with a sharp delivery that crashed into middle stump after Dogra played inside the line.That double blow broke the chase. With Mukesh and Akash Deep operating at full tilt, RoI bowled J&K out for 111 in 28.4 overs to complete a thumping 167-run win and claim the Irani Cup for the 33rd time — their first title since the 2023-24 season.Mukesh was outstanding, finishing with 6/33 in 10.4 overs. Akash Deep, returning from a seven-month injury lay-off, was equally incisive, taking 3/25 in nine overs. The two India pacers shared nine wickets as J&K collapsed from 54/0, losing 10-57.For Mukesh, match figures of 8/121 on a seaming surface were a timely reminder to the national selectors of his ability to exploit helpful conditions, especially with India’s New Zealand tour ahead.Akash Deep, too, strengthened his case, finishing with match figures of 6/78 after taking 3/43 in the first innings.Pant, though unable to field due to illness, appeared pleased while lifting the trophy — a fitting birthday gift on the day he turned 29. There’s also a possibility that he could miss Delhi’s Ranji opener vs Bengal on Oct 11.J&K had begun brightly through openers Shubham Khajuria (36) and Qamran Iqbal (32), who added 54 runs off 61 balls. Akash broke the stand by trapping Iqbal lbw before Mukesh’s burst changed the game.Mukesh later had wicket-keeper Kanhaiya Wadhawan caught behind for 2 and then cleaned up the tail in the 29th over, removing Abid Mushtaq, Umar Nazir and Sunil Kumar to finish the job.The third seamer, Mukesh Choudhary, also had a strong match, taking 5/47 in the first innings and six wickets overall.RoI’s biggest match-winner, however, was Ravichandran Smaran. The No. 6 batter was rightly named Player of the Match for his superb knocks of 68 and 135, the second innings century proving decisive in setting up the win.Earlier, RoI, resuming on 306/8, were bowled out for 319. Smaran, the last man dismissed, fell to Sunil Kumar, who finished with 3/56.J&K, who missed swing bowler Auqib Nabi, will need to regroup quickly before beginning their Ranji Trophy title defence against Madhya Pradesh at home from Oct 11.Rest of India 237 and 319 (R Smaran 135; S Kumar 3-56) beat Jammu & Kashmir 278 and 111 (S Khajuria 36, Mukesh Kumar 6-33) by 167 runs.
Article Summary: Rest of India beat Jammu & Kashmir by 167 runs to win the Irani Cup. RoI bowled J&K out for 111 in 28.4 overs to complete a thumping win. Ravichandran Smaran was named Player of the Match.

Article Text:

Looking back on his career

English fast bowler Craig Miles has announced his retirement from professional cricket at the age of 32, saying he needs to step away to protect his mental health.Miles, who last played in June during the Vitality Blast, finishes a 15-year career with more than 500 wickets across formats.In an open letter published by Gloucestershire, Miles explained that his recent struggles with cricket had become too difficult to manage."It’s with sadness, but also with huge pride, that I can announce my retirement from professional cricket. Although this has by no means been an easy decision, given the struggles I've experienced with the game in recent times, I've made this call in order to prioritise my mental well-being," he wrote."My recent time away from the game has given me the opportunity to reflect and understand myself better, as well as my relationship with cricket. The challenges I've faced recently are ones I've experienced at other points in my career, although never with the same intensity as this time. The high expectations I place on myself and the standards I've always tried to reach, have often been the catalyst for these periods."At times, they have compromised how I've felt about my abilities and performances. The questioning and self-doubt that follow only serve to reinforce an unhelpful narrative. When you add in the volatility and uncertainty that cricket naturally brings, it becomes an unforgiving and ultimately unsustainable way to approach the game."Miles said he no longer felt capable of maintaining the standards he expected from himself, despite having enjoyed many successful periods in the sport."Unfortunately, I now feel I no longer have the capacity to continue in a way that allows me to train, play and perform to a standard I can accept from myself. Of course, there have also been so many periods when I’ve loved the game, played with freedom and truly expressed the player I am.“A first-class debut at 16, more than 200 games, over 500 wickets, a One Day Cup and a Championship win - it’s been a pretty good go. I can appreciate those accomplishments more than ever now and, perhaps for the first time, give myself the self-validation I deserve.”Gloucestershire director of cricket Jon Lewis called Miles' decision brave and said the club would fully support him as he moves away from professional cricket.
Article Summary: English fast bowler Craig Miles has announced his retirement from professional cricket at the age of 32. Miles says he needs to step away to protect his mental health. The 32-year-old finishes a 15-year career with more than 500 wickets across formats.

NEW DELHI: Rishabh Pant could not have asked for a better 29th birthday present. On a day when he missed the action because of fever, the Rest of India captain watched his teammates complete a stunning comeback against Jammu and Kashmir to reclaim the Irani Cup before joining the celebrations with the trophy and cake.Rest of India, after conceding a 41-run first-innings lead to the Ranji Trophy champions, bowled out J&K for just 111 in their chase of 279 on Sunday to seal a commanding 167-run victory at the Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium.Pant, who made 10 and eight in the match, did not take the field on the fourth day, with Sarfaraz Khan taking over as on-field captain. But his leadership was evident in the way Rest of India responded after falling behind early.Addressing his teammates after the victory, Pant said the squad had been driven by the desire to restore pride after going without the Irani Cup for two years.“Guys, great effort. In the last 5-7 days, we were discussing that let's play for the pride and let's play for our monogram. No matter what happens, especially in the first innings, they did a good batting effort and they took the first innings lead,” Pant said in a video posted by BCCI Domestic.“But, in the dressing room, whatever they do, we need to focus on ourselves. Obviously, most of the time, the game went in their favour.”The captain praised his teammates for refusing to let the match slip away.“One thing for sure, our Rest of India team, we didn't let it go. We just kept on fighting with every ounce of intensity we had. One day, one over, one ball at a time and, everyone contributed in their own way,” he said.“From last two years, we were not winning. But, we made sure that when we leave this ground, we put our name on the trophy as winners.”The celebrations became even more special with Pant’s birthday falling on the day of the triumph.In a video shared by BCCI Domestic, his teammates and coaches gathered around the wicketkeeper-batter and sang ‘Happy Birthday’ in chorus. Ground staff members also offered their blessings and wishes before Pant cut the cake and posed with the trophy alongside his teammates.“Thanks for the gift,” a smiling Pant said as the dressing-room celebrations continued.The captain also explained how a tactical adjustment in bowling helped turn the contest around.“Mostly the plan was to bowl fuller in the first innings. That was the conversation we had with the bowlers that we were like, we would back up the length,” Pant said at the post-match presentation.“That was something we wanted to correct in the second innings because we knew our bowlers were really good, but the problem was the first innings we bowled too much back of the length, and we corrected that and bowled fuller and fuller in the second innings.”Mukesh Kumar led the demolition with 6-33 as J&K collapsed after lunch.Pant also reserved special praise for young batter Ravichandran Smaran, who scored 68 in the first innings before producing a match-winning 135 in the second.“Today all the pieces fell in place, but at the same time, you know, like you mentioned, Smaran, the way he played in both innings, I think it was outstanding innings, especially we were under pressure, especially in the second innings the way he played, it was outstanding,” Pant said.
Article Summary: Rest of India captain Rishabh Pant celebrates 29th birthday with Irani Cup win. Rest of India bowled out J&K for just 111 in chase of 279 to seal 167-run victory. Pant: 'We just kept on fighting with every ounce of intensity we had'

Article Title: 'It's like water to a thirsty person': Asian Games gold reignites women's hockey at grassroots
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

KOLKATA: The Indian women’s hockey team’s Asian Games gold medal after a 44-year wait has done more than secure direct qualification for the Olympics.According to coaches who have nurtured generations of players across the country, the triumph has rekindled belief at the grassroots, and is destined to inspire a new generation of girls to take up the sport while validating decades of hard work in academies and training centres, far from the spotlight.Former India captain Pritam Siwach, who has been working as a coach for more than 25 years in Sonipat, Haryana, believes the impact of the victory extends well beyond the podium.“This victory has given women’s hockey a new lease of life. It is like giving water to a thirsty person. Winning gold after 44 years has ended a long drought and brought renewed energy to the sport,” she said, adding that the success has given women’s hockey the recognition it deserves after years of operating in the shadow of the men’s game.For coaches working at the grassroots level, the medal has become a powerful tool. Dasrath Mahato, the 69-year-old from Khunti in Jharkhand who discovered and mentored Nikki Pradhan, said every major success creates a ripple effect among young athletes.“When children see players returning home with medals, they start to believe they can do the same. It inspires them to work harder and pursue hockey seriously,” Mahato said.The success has also been celebrated by coaches who have worked in some of the country’s leading hockey centres. Madhya Pradesh Hockey Academy coach Vandana says achievements at the elite level invariably strengthen the grassroots ecosystem.“When a sport performs well at the top level, it benefits the grassroots. We are already seeing more academies and leagues being established for women, and success like this will only accelerate that growth,” said Vandana, who trained the likes of Sushila Chanu and Bichu Devi Kharibam.Former India goalkeeper and coach Edgar Mascarenhas, who worked extensively in Odisha, described the achievement as one of the biggest milestones in the history of Indian women’s hockey.“I watched every match and what impressed me most was their fighting spirit. Even in difficult situations, they never gave up,” said Mascarenhas.The direct Olympic qualification has also been highlighted as one of the competition’s biggest outcomes. Coaches unanimously agreed that avoiding the pressure of an additional qualification campaign allows the team to focus entirely on preparation for the Games.“This may actually be even more important than the gold medal itself,” said Siwach. “Now the players know they are going to the Olympics and can devote all their energy towards preparing for that challenge.”The impact has been felt in regions that have emerged as strong contributors to Indian women’s hockey. In Mizoram, where coach Miss Btei helped nurture internationals Lalremsiami and Lalthantluangi, interest in the sport continues to grow among young children.“The success of players from our state will encourage more youngsters to take up hockey. Children see what Lalremsiami has achieved and begin to believe they can follow the same path,” she said.According to Btei, players as young as nine or ten years old, are now entering the development pathway with the latest generation already benefiting from the visibility created by the national team’s success.For former India international and coach Ajit Lakra, the gold medal represents proof that India’s grassroots structures are delivering results.“These players came through the grassroots system and delivered a gold-medal performance that resonated across Asia. It shows young athletes that there is a pathway from the grassroots level to the international stage,” said Lakra, who coached Rutuja Dadaso Pisal.While they welcomed the growing number of opportunities for women, the coaches stressed the importance of greater investment in infrastructure, academies and player development programmes to sustain the momentum.Yet the overriding sentiment remains one of optimism. Whether in hockey strongholds like Jharkhand and Odisha, established academies in Madhya Pradesh or emerging centres like Mizoram, coaches see the medal as a catalyst for growth.
Article Summary: The Indian women's hockey team's Asian Games gold medal after a 44-year wait has done more than secure direct qualification for the Olympics. The triumph has rekindled belief at the grassroots, and is destined to inspire a new generation of girls to take up the sport.

Article Title: Asian Games: Japan signs off, Doha takes the 2030 baton

NAGOYA: It has been a testing three weeks for Japan. Accommodation woes, transport and logistical nightmares, mismanagement and weather that refused to cooperate – the challenges the Asian Games organisers faced were plenty.Yet, as the Games drew to a close, there was enough to celebrate. Records were broken, medals won, friendships forged and, on Sunday, the baton was passed to Doha as Japan bid farewell to representatives from 44 countries at the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium.India finished fourth in the medals tally, while China topped the standings by a distance, collecting 341 medals, including an astonishing 169 golds.Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani described the Games as an event that would “shape the next generation of Asian sport” before welcoming the next chapter to his home country.“Tonight, as we lower the flag on Aichi-Nagoya 2026, we close these Games, but we raise the bar for Asian sport,” he said.“Over 350 records have been broken, including more than 50 world records.
